title: Lemon and Mascarpone Gelato
changes_from_base: Lemon peel infused in the milk and cold mascarpone whisked into a 4-yolk custard replace the pistachio milk; no cornflour.
summary: A silky, sunny gelato: milk infused with lemon peel, cooked into a light yolk custard and enriched with cold mascarpone, then sharpened with fresh lemon juice at the churn.

ingredients.item: unwaxed lemons, zest pared in wide strips
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Warm the milk with the lemon peel until it steams, then take it off the heat, cover and leave for 20 min so the oils flavour the milk. Lift out the peel.

steps.title: Yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt in the heatproof bowl until thick and pale.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Rewarm the lemon milk to steaming and pour about a third of it slowly onto the yolks, whisking all the time, then tip everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat, scraping the base, until the custard coats the spatula and reaches 77-80 °C, 5-8 min. Do not let it boil.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Sieve into the bowl over iced water and stir until cool. Whisk the cold mascarpone in the bowl with a ladle of custard until smooth, then whisk it into the rest. Cover and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Stir in the lemon juice, then churn for 20-25 min until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container, cover the surface with baking paper and freeze for at least 3 h. Leave it in the fridge for 15 min before scooping.

tips: Pare only the yellow peel; the white pith makes the custard bitter.
Add the lemon juice to the cold custard, never the hot one, or it may curdle.
Serve with crisp almond biscuits or fresh raspberries.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10-15 min in the fridge before scooping.
